explanation: It moves only diagonally, which never changes the colour of its square. Each player's two bishops start on opposite colours, so one is called light-squared and the other dark-squared.

claims.text: In chess, the bishop is the only piece that stays on squares of one colour for the whole game.
Rooks, knights and queens can each move between light and dark squares.
A bishop moves only diagonally, and a diagonal move never changes the colour of the square.
Each player's two bishops start on squares of opposite colours and are called the light-squared and dark-squared bishops.

evidence.restatement: A bishop moves only along diagonals, so it never leaves the colour of square it starts on. Knights, rooks, queens, kings and pawns all reach both colours.
Rook, knight and queen each have moves that switch square colour (a one-square rook step, any knight move, any one-square queen step).
One diagonal step always lands on a square of the same colour, however many steps follow.
Each side's bishops start on one dark and one light square (c1 and f1 for White) and are named after their square colour.
